content.raw:
Short answer: Good lymphedema self-care is simple but consistent: protect the skin, use prescribed compression, keep moving, monitor changes, and seek early treatment for infection or sudden worsening.

Clinically reviewed by Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, Plastic, Reconstructive & Lymphedema Surgeon in Singapore. Last reviewed: August 2026. This article is for education only and does not replace personalised medical assessment.

Core self-care habits

  • wear prescribed compression as advised;
  • moisturise and inspect skin regularly;
  • treat cuts, fungal infection and wounds early;
  • move daily and progress exercise gradually;
  • avoid sudden overload of the affected limb;
  • keep follow-up with therapists or doctors when symptoms change.

Skin care and infection prevention

Skin breaks can trigger cellulitis. Patients should manage athlete’s foot, insect bites, scratches and wounds promptly, especially if they have had previous infections.

Compression

Compression should fit properly. A garment that causes pain, numbness, colour change, rolling bands or wounds should be reviewed.

Tracking changes

Useful signs to track include swelling pattern, heaviness, garment fit, infection episodes, wounds, pain and impact on daily activities.

Frequently asked questions

Can self-care cure lymphedema?

No. It helps control symptoms and reduce complications.

What is the most important habit?

Skin protection and consistent compression are often central, but the plan should be individualised.

When should I seek review?

Seek review for recurrent cellulitis, sudden swelling, wounds, pain or worsening despite good self-care.

Related surgical guide: If swelling remains persistent despite appropriate conservative care, or if recurrent cellulitis is a major issue, read LVA surgery in Singapore: lymphovenous bypass for lymphedema.
